note: A CISO does not think 'show me vendor escalations'. They think 'what is overdue', 'what changed under me', 'what is unowned'. Triggers cluster across producers, and the clustering is DATA rather than logic: a new trigger lands in a cluster by declaration. An unmapped trigger surfaces in an explicit `unclustered` group and is never silently dropped — evals/clusters.sh asserts that every trigger the shipped producers can emit has a home here, and that an unknown one still appears.
orderNote: Clusters are presented in this order. It is a judgement about what a person should read first, written down as chosen: a clock that has run out is already late, whereas an uncontrolled exposure is a standing condition. It is NOT a ranking of the items inside them, and there is no number anywhere.

clusters.title: Clocks running out
clusters.meaning: A period the organisation set, or a regulator set, has passed or is about to.

clusters.title: Something moved under us
clusters.meaning: A fact an earlier judgement rested on has changed since that judgement was made. These are the ones nobody reports, because nothing failed.

clusters.title: Nobody owns it
clusters.meaning: There is no name attached, or no answer to what this holds up. Every other escalation has to land on somebody; these are the ones that cannot.

clusters.title: We disagree with ourselves
clusters.meaning: Two records about the same thing say different things. Reported, never resolved — which of them is wrong is a human's call.

clusters.title: Uncontrolled exposure
clusters.meaning: Something is exposed and nothing is recorded against it. A standing condition rather than a deadline, which is why it does not sit under the clocks.

clusters.title: Over tolerance
clusters.meaning: Past a line the organisation itself drew, and still there.

addedAfterDesign.note: The design spec's cluster table was written before ai-register shipped its final trigger set. Checking the mapping against what the producers actually emit found three with no home. Recorded here rather than folded in silently, because the gap is the argument for the unclustered group existing at all.

triggers.autonomy-increased: moved-under-us — the deployment can reach more than it could when it was assessed
triggers.provider-arrangement-missing: unowned — the contractual questions this raises have nowhere to be asked
triggers.evidence-expired: clocks-running-out — the artifact holding up a satisfied requirement has run out
triggers.review-overdue: clocks-running-out — a policy review date the organisation set has passed. Beside revalidation-overdue and assessment-overdue, which are the same shape: an interval somebody chose, and nobody kept.
triggers.superseded-only: uncontrolled-exposure — every policy aimed at a requirement has been superseded and nothing approved replaced it. A standing condition rather than a deadline, which is this cluster's own definition. Its sibling `draft-only` is deliberately NOT here and not a trigger at all: the two share an end state — no approved document in force — and differ in whether the gap is VISIBLE. A draft shows as a draft; a requirement covered only by superseded documents looks populated. Deceptive escalates, visible does not.
triggers.method-prerequisite-unmet: self-disagreement — PROVISIONAL, filed as an open decision. Both v1 checks are one record contradicting another about the same analysis: the method says `quantitative` while settings record no currency, or `conformance: partial` stands beside an empty `deviations`. The cluster's own meaning — "which of them is wrong is a human's call" — is exactly the state, since nothing here can tell whether to change the method or set the currency. Placed rather than left unclustered so the run did not stall; placement is data and reversing it is a one-line change.
